messages:
elaine-support: Heads-up — acme-co escalated: SSO logins failing immediately after our IdP signing cert rollover (10:02 UTC). Customer sees 403 / InvalidRecipient in their SP logs. Says it started right after our rotation. Attaching our edge logs and a redacted SAMLResponse they sent.

josh-eng: Can you paste the SAMLResponse (redacted) and our edge error from the same window? Need the Recipient/AssertionConsumerServiceURL and the Subject/Issuer.

elaine-support: Paste below (redacted):
```
<SAMLResponse>...Recipient="https://app.acme-co/saml/consume"...Issuer="https://idp.customer-idp.com"...Signature>...</SAMLResponse>
Edge error: 403 InvalidRecipient: expected https://acme.example.com/_saml/acs but got https://app.acme-co/saml/consume
```

maya-sre: Interesting — our edge proxy rewrites host headers for customers behind shared routing. Did the ACS in the customer SAMLResponse match what our proxy forwarded to the origin? If the proxy rewrote the host, the SP validation can fail. Also saw a metadata refresh job around the same time returning `Content-Encoding: gzip` and `Content-Length` mismatch. Could be truncated metadata XML -> signature parsing fails and fallback picks wrong cert.

ivan-security: Two things to check: 1) IdP metadata we have cached (thumbprint) vs metadata fetched at rotation time; 2) whether the customer SP is using an ACS alias that we should accept. Run: `curl -v -H "Accept-Encoding: identity" https://idp.customer-idp.com/metadata` and compare the KeyDescriptor X509Certificate thumbprint with the cert in our DB.

deploy-bot: [deploy] idp-metadata-updater v2.14 deployed @ 1768909000 — fetched metadata for idp.customer-idp.com, updated cert thumbprint, TTL 24h.

josh-eng: If the metadata fetch returned gzipped content but our metadata parser assumed identity, it could have stored a corrupted XML and extracted the wrong KeyDescriptor (or none). That explains signature/recipient mismatch if we also fell back to a prior cached ACS url mapping. Workaround: force metadata re-fetch with `Accept-Encoding: identity` + bump cache version.

maya-sre: I'll flush the CDN edge cache and force the metadata updater to re-fetch with identity header now. Running: `kubectl exec -it metadata-updater -- curl -v -H "Accept-Encoding: identity" https://idp.customer-idp.com/metadata` then validate.

elaine-support: I'll tell acme-co: we found a metadata ingestion edge-case during our cert roll — asking them to retry SSO after 10m and send one more SAMLResponse if it still fails. Also requested their ACS exact value and RelayState from their administrator.

ivan-security: After re-fetch we should compare thumbprints: `sha1sum cert.pem` vs our stored thumbprint. If mismatch, revert to accepting the old cert for a 12h grace window (temporary) while we coordinate rotation with their IdP.

josh-eng: Agreed. Long-term fix: make metadata updater respect `Content-Encoding` headers and validate Content-Length against decompressed size. Also add a metadata diff alert when cert thumbprint changes for an active customer (auto-ping support + account owner).

maya-sre: Done — cache flushed and metadata re-fetched with identity header. New metadata shows both old and new KeyDescriptor entries (good). Updated our DB thumbprint to include both. Pushed a hotfix to metadata-updater to prefer identity or fall back elegantly.

elaine-support: Confirmed with acme-co; login works now. They sent a sample SAMLResponse that validates. Marking escalated case resolved, will keep monitoring for 24h and follow up with postmortem. :white_check_mark:

josh-eng: Nice triage. Filing a short postmortem and a follow-up ticket to harden metadata ingestion.

deploy-bot: [ticket] created: SSO-2064 metadata parser robustification (assigned josh-eng)

ivan-security: Please add a note to the customer record about coordinated cert rotations and a recommended 1-hour overlap for old cert acceptance.

elaine-support: Will do. Thanks all :heart:
